title: Large liquid-scintillator detectors as high-energy recoil detectors: can Borexino, KamLAND, JUNO or SNO+ see the LZ models through 12C, 13C and 1H recoils?
question: For inelastic O1 (delta=300-380 keV), elastic L10/O6 at LZ's fit, SI reference and P058's exothermic chi2, what recoil rates, quenched energies, threshold pass/fail and 14C signal-to-background follow in Borexino (278 t), KamLAND (1 kt), SNO+ (780 t) and JUNO (20 kt)?
headline_result: No scintillator can test the LZ interpretations: delta=300-380 keV needs A>=97-126 (12C ceiling 40 keV); LZ's L10 fit gives 1.1e-7 proton recoils per t(H) yr and 0.8 13C recoils/yr in JUNO at 3-9 keVee; the only open channel, exothermic chi2 down-scattering (a line at E*~300-376 keV, 1.6-2.0e5 carbon recoils/yr in JUNO at P058's f2 limits, 12-20 keVee), sits 1e6 times under 14C (S/B 2e-6), below every threshold.
key_numbers: ceilings 1TeV: 1H 3.4, 12C 40.3, 13C 43.6, 16O 53.5 keV; A_min 97/115/120/126; L10: 1.1e-7 /t(H)/yr, 13C 3.9e-3 /t(13C)/yr, JUNO 0.80/yr; analytic/WimPyDD proton 0.94-0.97; exothermic C 4.3e7 /t/yr per unit coupling, kappa 7.5e-5/3.9e-3/0.048/1.5, R_ROI 926 (P058 916); JUNO at f2 limits 1.6-2.0e5 C, 64-88 H recoils/yr vs 7e10 14C in window; stat-only 1-yr reach 1.7-2.1x LZ (JUNO), 8-9x (Borexino); 1e-3 systematic -> 360-560x weaker
model_or_mechanism: kinematic ceilings; L10/O6 q^4 spin on free proton and 13C; exothermic O1 down-scattering on C/H/O with Birks quenching and 14C background
result_type: computed (kinematics, WimPyDD rates) / estimated (13C spin, quenching, thresholds, 14C)
confidence: medium - kinematics and rates validated to 1-6% against P012/P021/P058; detector response and 14C inputs recalled
